SHRI RAJMOHAN UNNITHAN (KASARAGOD): Thank you, Mr. Chairman, for giving me opportunity to speak on the Supplementary Demands for Grants. 

Sir, our economy is on the verge of collapse. I recall a cartoon drawn by Satish Acharya. In the cartoon, Prime Minister Modi ji is depicted as a chowkidar at an ATM, and people like Nirav Modi and Vijay Mallya are running away with money looted from the ATM. Meanwhile, chowkidar Modi ji is sleeping quietly and a poster is placed in front of him that reads, ‘In case of emergency, blame Nehru.” Sir, while this Government is indulging in Nehru-bashing and emotional blackmail of the people, it has failed miserably to save the economy of India.

India could overcome the Global Financial Crisis of 2008-09, widely referred to as ‘the Great Recession’, under the sagacious leadership of Shri Manmohan Singh, a great economist. But the present Government failed the economy with its myopic economics and unscientific measures like demonetization and hasty implementation of the GST. Unwise handling of the COVID-19 pandemic further aggravated the crumbling economy. The Government must issue a White Paper on impact of the demonetization on the Indian economy.

India is facing ‘New Brain Drain’ as skilled and educated young Indians are running away from India due to her poor economy and lack of employment. A recent report by Redseer Strategy Consultants predicted that close to 1.8 million Indians will spend 85 billion US dollars on pursuing a degree abroad by 2024. At present, 13.24 lakh students are studying in 79 countries, according to a Ministry of External Affairs report released in 2022.

Global ratings firm Moody’s has recently lowered India’s 2022 real GDP growth projections to 7.0 per cent from 7.7 per cent. “We expect growth to decelerate to 4.8 per cent in 2023”, the Moody’s said. “The downward revision assumes higher inflation, high interest rates and slowing global growth will dampen economic momentum by more than we had previously expected”, the Moody's forecasted.

Consumer food price inflation in India has increased from 0.68 per cent to 8.38 per cent between September 2021 and April 2022. The overall inflation rate was recently reported to be around seven per cent with most of the price rise stemming from high food and fuel prices. In Kerala, the price of all varieties of rice, staple food in the State, has doubled in a year. People will have to spend Rs. 2,400 crore extra a year on rice. Life of the common man has become miserable due to high inflation and unemployment.

In 2014, the Government of India launched its Make in India initiative as a part of India’s renewed focus on manufacturing. The ‘AtmaNirbhar Bharat’ campaign announced in 2020 was also intended to further boost local manufacturing under its stated goal of making India economically self-sufficient. But the Government could not make any headway in this sector mainly because of India’s poor infrastructure. India uses only three per cent of its GDP for infrastructure construction each year, as compared to China’s 20 per cent of its GDP.

The farming community is facing a severe crisis. The prices of cash crops are falling down. After a moderate post-pandemic revival, the price of natural rubber has crashed to a 16-month low of 150 per kilogram in the Indian market. The price of latex, which soared during the pandemic due to huge demand from glove makers, took a more severe drubbing with its prices rolling down below Rs.120.

The Government of India has discontinued the Railway Budget. So, it should be resumed. Kerala has very inadequate Railway infrastructure. Much awaited Kanhangad-Kaniyur railway line connecting Kanhangad, Kerala with Mysore and Bengaluru through Kaniyur, Karnataka, and the Sabari rail link connecting Angamali with Erumeli are still pending with the Southern Railway for approval. The construction of railway flyovers in North Malabar has commenced years back. In my constituency, Kasaragod, 10 such flyovers have been proposed. But still, all the work is progressing at a snail’s pace. The construction of some flyovers has not even started and other ROBs still await approval. The work of Nileshwaram Pallikkara ROB is in the final stage. Now the only thing left is to control the train traffic and to place the grids appropriately.

Unfortunately, it has been waiting for months for getting permission from the Ministry of Railways. Kannur International Airport has completed four years on 9th December, 2022. It is one of the most important airports of Kerala. We are sure that you are aware that Kannur has not been considered as a ‘point of call’ so far even though all the national carriers of GCC have repeatedly expressed their wish to have flights to Kannur. I would request you to kindly include Kannur International Airport also in the ‘point of call’ list for foreign airlines. Currently, only four Indian companies, namely, Air India, Air India Express, Go First, and Indigo are operating a handful of international and domestic flights. An instruction from the Government to all the airline companies in India to provide more services, both on international and domestic routes, will be highly appreciated. At present, Kannur Airport does not have any operation so far to countries in the East like Malaysia, Singapore, and Thailand, whereas Chennai and Mangalore airports are operating to these countries. My constituency, Kasargod, for the last few years, has been suffering from the disastrous effects of endosulfan pesticide. The endosulfan was spread over the cashew plantations in the district. In the last 23 years, since 1978, it has ruined 30 village panchayats and three municipal towns in the district. As per the Supreme Court directive, 6,727 persons were identified as the victims of endosulfan. I urge upon the Government to allocate sufficient funds to the Government of Kerala to rehabilitate endosulfan victims. In 2003, the Government of India had announced PMSSY, Prime Minister Swasthya Suraksha Yojana, which aimed at correcting regional imbalance in the availability of affordable, reliable, tertiary healthcare services. New AIIMS’ were planned under PMSSY. Kerala deserves an AIIMS which could be set up in Kasargod district, which is the most backward district in terms of the health infrastructure.

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Thank you. Please conclude.

SHRI RAJMOHAN UNNITHAN: National Highway 66 is already causing many traffic issues in my constituency Kasargod. I would like to mention some of the grievances of the people of Kasargod with regard to the National Highway underpass.… (Interruptions) We require an underpass at Periya, Madeena Mill Junction, Anangoor Junction, Mavunkal Junction, Indira Nagar, Edakkattuvayal, Pervadu, Muttam Gate, Hidayath Nagar and Kaikamba. With these words, I conclude my speech.

SHRI K. SUBBARAYAN (TIRUPPUR): Hon Chairman Sir, Vanakkam.

In our county MSMEs which provide a good number of employment opportunities are in a dying state. Hosiery Industry is very much affected in Tiruppur district of my constituency. Almost 30 per cent of them have been closed due to the wrong economic policies of the Union Government. Remaining 70 per cent of this Industry is in critical condition facing difficulties. I wish to state that the policies of the present Government should be changed. Tiruppur is producing and supplying garments including T-shirts for use in India and for exporting to almost all the countries in the five continents of the world. But the Union Government is importing T-shirts from Bangladesh. 

The Union Government has not even understood the internal situation in our country. They are not even bothered about the domestic production whereas they are interested in importing from a foreign country. Union Government has not understood the seriousness of this matter. 

We have to protect the Knitwear Industry of India which is exporting to all the countries in the world. Every year through this knitwear industry, Indian Government earns many thousands of crores of foreign exchange. I urge upon the Union Government that a sizeable portion of the foreign exchange generated by this knitwear industry should be allocated for improving the infrastructure of Tiruppur city and Tiruppur district. 

Similarly, a special fund should be allocated for Tiruppur, as it is earning foreign exchange to our country besides providing employment to many thousands of people belonging to north India. Tiruppur is also providing employment to several thousands of people belonging to the southern districts of Tamil Nadu. Is the Union Government concerned about Tiruppur or not? Does the Union Government have the responsibility to protect Tiruppur or not? 

The Union Government is not at all bothered about protecting and developing Tiruppur which provides ample employment to a sizeable population of our country. I urge that the Union Government should have to show more concern towards Tiruppur. Road infrastructure and connectivity have to be improved in Tiruppur as thousands of foreigners pay visit to this place. Traffic congestion is also causing problem. Roads have to be upgraded. I urge that a special fund of Rs 250 Crore should be allocated by the Union Government for expanding and providing a better infrastructure in Tiruppur. 

GST dues for Tamil Nadu are to be released soon. This Union Government is ruling under the motto “Satyameva Jayate” –“Truth alone triumphs”. It is favouring the States ruled by them with more allocation of funds. Whereas there is less allocation of funds to the Opposition ruled States in the country. This is injustice. You are preaching justice to all. But your act shows you are partial. I therefore urge upon you for releasing adequate funds for meeting the demands of Tamil Nadu. Thank you. 

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Thank you.

Shri K. Navaskani Ji -- Not Present. 

Shri S. Venkatesan.

SHRI S. VENKATESAN (MADURAI): Hon Chairman Sir, Vanakkam. 

Thank you for this opportunity to speak on Supplementary Demands for Grants. We have been time and again raising questions about setting up of AIIMS in Madurai. But whenever we raised such a question hon. Union Ministers replied in this House about the time by when the construction work of this AIIMS would be completed. The Union Minister even told us in this House yesterday that construction work relating to AIIMS in Madurai will be completed by October 2026. We are not asking about the date of completion of this AIIMS project. We want to know by when you will start the construction work of AIIMS in Madurai? Nobody in this world has found the technology to complete anything without even starting that project. I urge upon the Union Minister that he should inform in this House that by when the construction work as regards AIIMS in Madurai will be started. We the Opposition parties are pleading to kindly start implementation of the project for which the foundation stone was laid by hon. Prime Minister. As part of deceiving Tamil Nadu, I should say you are not starting the work relating to construction of AIIMS in Madurai. 

Scholarships for students from Class I to Class VIII of SC, ST and minority communities, Beedi workers and the disabled persons have been stopped. On one side you are so generous towards funding the corporate companies. You are not collecting back the loans given to corporate companies. You declare such loans as NPAs. You are showing your loyalty towards corporate companies. We urge you to show such loyalty towards education sector also. Village development funds were released to the villages through a Scheme called ‘New Agreement for Villages’. Now the name has been changed in Hindi as ‘Gram Uday Se Bharat Uday’. There is a saying in Tamil. “You have given a name; but have you provided food?” You have just given a new name but you have even reduced the actual allocation of funds for that Scheme. 

Similarly, funds are not allocated for the railways projects meant for Tamil Nadu. This is a completely deceiving act. You are not even allocating to Southern Railway an amount equal to one-fourth of the funds allocated to the railway projects of Northern and North Eastern Railways. We urge that funds should be increased for Southern Railways after the present discussion. 

Divyang – which means the children of God- is a Sanskrit name given to disabled persons. But you have made a reduction of 30 percent of funds allocated for children of God- Divyang persons. It is pretty clear that you not providing justice to humans as well as Gods. As mentioned by the hon. MP from Tiruppur, the textile industry is facing severe crisis. 

Collateral free loans should be provided. There was an announcement made 10 years ago about setting up of a National Institute for Pharmaceutical Education and Research (NIPER) in Madurai. You are refusing to allocate funds for the setting up of NIPER. This decision to set up NIPER was taken by the then Union Cabinet. But you are not willing to implement the decision of the Union Cabinet. I urge that the construction work should be started for the setting up of NIPER in Madurai. 

Similarly, the airport at Madurai should be operational round the clock with adequate security and necessary powers. I urge that GST dues that are pending for Tamil Nadu should also be released very soon by this Union Government. Thank you.

SHRI RAM MOHAN NAIDU KINJARAPU (SRIKAKULAM): Thank you very much, Chairman Sir, for giving me an opportunity to speak on Supplementary Demands for Grants. Since the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, you have also been a witness to this, whenever there has been a discussion on Budget, we have always been demanding for the assurances that have been mentioned in the Act and it is not just that we have been constantly repeating. The Central Government also has to understand the reason for us to constantly repeat our demands regarding the AP Reorganization Act, which is that most of them have been unfulfilled till now. That is why, once again, I would request the Central Government to fulfil all the assurances that have been mentioned in the AP Reorganization Act.

I want to briefly highlight some of them. Some have already been mentioned by my colleague Jayadev Galla Ji yesterday in his Speech in the Supplementary Demands for Grants. One of the most important demands is the establishment of a Railway Zone. This has been the long pending demand and we felt very happy when it was mentioned in the AP Reorganization Act. It was announced three and a half years ago by the Central Government themselves. But even today, when Rs. 170 crore has been budgeted for the creation of Vizag Railway Zone and also new Rayagada Division, only Rs. 106 crore has been sanctioned. I have to mention on the floor of the House that the people of Uttara Andhra who are going to be major beneficiaries of the Railway Zone are not satisfied with the sanction. We want to see the Zone in action. Only then, there will be the fulfilment of this Railway Zone. For that, we request the Central Government to fulfil all the budgetary requirements for the creation of a new Railway zone in the State of Andhra Pradesh. 

I do not know why there has been an unjustified decision to remove Waltair Division completely. It was one of the most profitable Divisions in the country. Without any solid reason and without any solid justification, they are simply removing the Waltair Division which is not right. So, once again, I want to demand the Central Government to include Waltair Division in its entirety and to continue its existence in the South Coast Railway Zone which has been announced. 

Also, some stations like Palasa, Mandasa, Summadevi, Baruva, Sompeta, Jhadupudi, Ichchapuram come under Khurda Road Division. I would like to request the Central Government also to include them in the South Coast Railway Zone. These might be something related to the Railway Ministry but whenever any decision has to be made, it has financial implications which is why I want to mention in the Supplementary Demands for Grants also. 

Like I have said, the creation of Railway Zone has been the dream of Uttara Andhra people. New Railway lines, new trains, new station developments and new infrastructure – this is going to help in the economic development especially of Uttara Andhra region. So, without any further delay, let the Central Government bring the zone into existence and into operation. That is my strong demand to the Central Government through my Speech. 

Now, I come to the issue of Vizag Steel Plant. Not just this, the Central Government has been constantly deciding on privatising many of the PSUs. If there is a reasoning, the first and foremost reason that they give is that it is not the business of the Government to deal with these kinds of PSUs. 

Sir, there are hundreds of PSUs in this country. If such a reasoning is made by saying that it is not our business to get into the working of the PSUs, then you first pick up unprofitable units and start privatizing them. It will make some sense. But Vizag Steel Plant is one of the most profitable units in the country. 

17.00 hrs

Steel is such a strategic asset for this country. You cannot depend upon other countries when it is such an important major attribute in the nation building of this country. You have seen from the Russia-Ukraine war crisis and also in Europe as to how much Europe is dependent on China also and suddenly they are facing a crisis right now and we are speaking about Atmanirbhar Bharat. Then it does not make any sense that a steel plant, which has a great potential like the Vizag Steel Plant, is being privatised. Even after the announcement of privatisation, it has been going into profits. With the working of the labour there who are dependent on that, it is one of the most profitable units today. So, there is no reason to privatise the Vizag Steel Plant. I would request and demand the Central Government to rethink on its decision.

Along with this, there are some issues regarding the employees of the Vizag Steel Plant. After the disinvestment decision, promotions and filling up of the vacancies have been stalled for the last two years. It is a separate thing that it might happen or it might not happen but why should they stop the filling up of the vacancies or recruitment or promotions? This is not right. 

Also, there are displaced persons who have donated their land for the creation of steel plant. For several years, they are waiting for employment. Approximately 8300 people are still not employed. Who is going to take care of these people? This question has to be answered by the Central Government. 

Sir, I come from the State of Andhra Pradesh. The finances of the State are in a very alarming situation right now. We are in a position where the Government is not even able to pay the salaries on time. Today is 12th of the month and there are a lot of Government employees who have not received their salaries which is very alarming. I would like to ask one question to the Central Government. When a State in this great nation is facing this kind of a financial crisis, is the Central Government just going to spectate or going to just look at the functioning of the State or is it going to interfere? There are many other issues also linked with it, if you go deeper into it. NREGA funds have been misappropriated. We have given a complaint. Out of Rs.231 crore, only Rs. 5 crore have been recovered. We do not know what is happening. C&AG also reported that on Rs. 48,000 crore, there are no receipts at all.

The 15th Finance Commission grants have to go directly to the panchayats. It is a very good decision which the Central Government has taken so that the panchayats are strengthened. Now funds amounting to approximately Rs. 900 crore are not going to the panchayats. The sarpanches are paying from their pockets for sanitation, electricity, etc. This is also not right. The Centre has to interfere in it. 

Disaster Relief Fund to the tune of Rs. 1100 crore are unutilised and misappropriated. What is the Central Government going to do about it? These are funds which the Central Government is sending to the States. When the finances of the State are not happening in the right way, then who is going to take the responsibility? I would request the hon. Finance Minister to answer these questions. Thank you, Sir.  

DR. THOL THIRUMAAVALAVAN (CHIDAMBARAM): Hon Chairman Sir, Vanakkam. Thank you for this opportunity to speak on the Supplementary Demands for Grants.

Poverty, unemployment, and inflation are on the rise and hence price rise, the resultant of which, is affecting the poor and working class people of the country. Due to the wrong economic policies and financial mismanagement of the Union Government, economic recession has taken place in our country. When you compare the Indian rupee with that of the US dollar, the value of the Indian currency has declined so much and it has gone so deep. I wish to state that the BJP led Union Government should be held responsible for this.

Tamil Nadu is in the first and foremost place among the States in the collection of revenues for this Union Government. But as per the devolution of funds for the States by the Union, Tamil Nadu gets a very less amount as its share. We have doubts whether the Union Government is doing this intentionally?

Whether it is a railway project or any other Project, the Union Government of India, is either deceiving or boycotting Tamil Nadu. There was an announcement regarding setting up of AIIMS in Madurai. The hon. Prime Minister had even laid the foundation stone. It is a matter of shame to state that there is no progress in the execution of work relating to construction of AIIMS in Madurai. It is a matter of pain and shame, that a Scheme like AIIMS, launched by the hon.. Prime Minister in Madurai has not seen the light of the day. I urge that there should be an official announcement from the Government as regards starting the construction work of AIIMS in Madurai.

The Fifteenth Finance Commission has framed guidelines as regards the devolution of funds to the States. This guideline states that the devolution will be as per the population of 2011 Census, due to which Tamil Nadu is affected. I should say that Tamil Nadu is the only State which prudently implemented the family planning programme of the Government of India. Tamil Nadu controlled its population. In Uttar Pradesh, family planning programme was not properly implemented and as a result there is an increase in the population of that State whereas Tamil Nadu has controlled its population by sincerely implementing the family planning programme of the Government of India. As population is taken as a criterion for devolution of funds, Tamil Nadu is very much affected. The Union Government should come forward to allocate more funds to Tamil Nadu as the State is contributing much to the Union’s share of money by way of tax and other collection.

The Government of India has given an assurance for allocating funds for a Defence Corridor in Tamil Nadu. Tank factory situated in Avadi should be expanded. Although the Union Government assured to provide money for expansion of a Defence Corridor in Tamil Nadu, only a paltry sum is allocated in the Budget. 

Every time they give an assurance for linking the rivers of the country – an announcement was even made regarding Godavari-Pennaru-Cauvery linking Scheme – but no fund was allocated. I, on behalf of Viduthalai Siruthaigal Party, urge that necessary funds should be allocated for this Scheme.

It is very much evident that poverty alleviation is not in the scheme of things of this Government. During the year 2020, as many as 4.6 crore people have been newly included in the list of poor people. This is due to the wrong economic policies of the Union Government. 

A report says that if the wealth tax for the 98 percent of the richest persons in India, is increased by just 4 per cent, we can run the midday meal scheme throughout the country for next 17 years. Therefore, their wealth tax should not be reduced, rather enhanced.

I put forth one important demand for making Vande Bharat Train service operational between Chennai and Madurai.

Thank you.

KUMARI RAMYA HARIDAS (ALATHUR): Sir, I am thankful to you for giving me this opportunity to participate in this discussion. It is really unfortunate that the last Budget did not mention anything about new railway lines or new trains for Kerala. I have raised this issue several times in this House for a weekly train connecting the pilgrimage areas like Palani and Rameshwaram. But there has been no positive reply from the Government. 

I have mentioned several times about Vallathol Nagar Railway Station which is named after the famous national poet and freedom fighter, Padma Bhushan Vallathol Narayana Menon. The condition of this Railway Station is very pathetic. There should be an allocation of fund to renovate this Railway Station. I also submitted several proposals to construct ROBs and FOBs in different areas in my constituency. But I did not get any response.

In agricultural sector, the allocation in the Budget was not adequate for paddy. I pointed out several times that the assistance for support price should be increased. But there was no such increased allocation. 

Sir, Kerala is the second largest producer of milk next to Haryana. But there is a lack of notable assistance for any project from the Central Government to help dairy farmers. I request the hon. Finance Minister to please consider this sector also. 

Sir, Midday Meal Program is the backbone of school education, especially, in primary school education. But the allocation or the assistance for the Midday Meal Programme is not sufficient as there is price hike for all the commodities. So, the allocation for Midday meal assistance to States should be increased as per the present scenario. 

MGNREGS is the prime economic source of common people in rural and urban areas but if we see the allocation of fund for the Financial Year 2021-22, the fund allocated under this Scheme is not sufficient. The new guidelines to cut short the working days and projects should be revised. This project must be considered as one of the important projects for the eradication of poverty and it should be given worthful attention.

Sir, as we all know, the MSME sector is the major victim during the COVID-19 pandemic years. Most of the MSMEs were closed and stopped working permanently. The assistance for such MSMEs was not included in the Budget. Even the writing off of interest during the pandemic period has not been considered. I request here to consider writing off interest and allot extra financial assistance under a special subsidy scheme to strengthen these MSMEs.

As far as the health sector in our area is concerned, Palakkad Medical College is the major hospital. The State Government is also providing whatever assistance they can to run this hospital. Even the Members of Legislative Assemblies are contributing their local area development fund for this Medical College but it is not sufficient to make it a main centre. Several people from my constituency are also depending on this medical college. I request the hon. Health Minister as well as the hon. Finance Minister to grant special Central fund for establishing a critical unit in this medical college. 

Thank you very much, Sir. 

श्री रितेश पाण्डेय (अम्बेडकर नगर) : आदरणीय अधिष्ठाता महोदय, आपका बहुत-बहुत धन्यवाद।

महोदय, मैं मात्र दो मिनट में अपनी बातें कहूंगा। यह सत्य है कि जो डिमांड्स फॉर ग्रांट्स, जो अनुपूरक अनुदानों की मांगें आई हुई हैं, इनमें कुछ जन कल्याणकारी योजनाओं के लिए धन बढ़ाने का काम किया गया है। उनमें से कई रूरल डेवलपमेंट की योजनाएं हैं, होम मिनिस्ट्री के खर्चे हैं, केमिकल्स-फर्टिलाइजर्स और रोड एंड ट्रांसपोर्ट की योजनाएं हैं। यह अत्यंत ही जरूरी है कि एक इकोनॉमी के लिए, एक अर्थव्यवस्था के लिए इन क्षेत्रों में और मांगों को पूरा किया जाए। 

मैं उत्तर प्रदेश से आता हूं। उत्तर प्रदेश हमारे देश का सबसे बड़ा सूबा है। यहां लगभग 22 करोड़ से अधिक की आबादी रहती है। जायज सी बात है कि यहां नौजवानों के बहुत से मुद्दे हैं। नौजवानों की अपने रोजगार को लेकर बहुत सारी अपेक्षाएं हैं। खास तौर से ये अपेक्षाएं फाइनेंस मिनिस्ट्री से और इस सरकार से हैं। 

मैं यहां पर इनके बारे में बताना चाहता हूं और कुछ आंकड़े भी पेश करना चाहता हूं। कहीं न कहीं अनइंप्लॉयमेंट के बारे में हमारे तमाम साथियों ने बताया कि वह आठ प्रतिशत को छूने का काम कर रहा है। यह अत्यंत ही चिंताजनक है, लेकिन क्या सरकार ने अपनी अनुपूरक अनुदानों की मांगों को लेकर इन विषयों के ऊपर कोई डिमांड्स फॉर ग्रांट्स एलोकेट नहीं की हैं? यह भी अत्यंत ही चिंताजनक है।

अभी आंकड़ों के हिसाब से हम देखते हैं कि जो एकलव्य रेसिडेंशियल स्कूल्स हैं, इनके अंदर चार हजार टीचरों को नौकरियां दे रखी हैं। इनमें 11 हजार टीचरों की जगह बनाकर रखी गई थी, लेकिन मात्र चार हजार टीचर्स ही इंप्लॉयड हैं। कौशल विकास योजना के अंतर्गत हमने यह देखा है कि मात्र 72 परसेंट फंड को यूटिलाइज किया जाता है और जो प्लेसमेंट्स हैं, वे भी बहुत कम हैं। जिन दूसरे पॉइंट्स पर यह स्कीम आई थी, उनमें 90 लाख लोगों में से मात्र 20 लाख लोगों को ही नौकरियां मिल पाईं, प्लेसमेंट्स मिल पाए।  

जो इसका थर्ड फेज़ आया था, उसमें चार लाख लोगों को ट्रेन किया गया था, जिनमें से मात्र 30 हजार लोगों को नौकरियां मिल पाईं। यह दिखाता है कि कहीं न कहीं नौजवानों के मुद्दे इस सरकार के एजेंडे में पीछे हैं। … (व्यवधान) मैं कनक्लूड कर रहा हूं। 

HON. CHAIRPERSON: Hon. Member, please conclude. 

SHRI RITESH PANDEY: Sir, I am just concluding with my final words. I know that you have given me the time and I am very thankful to you. I am concluding. सर, मैं अपनी बात खत्म कर रहा हूं। … (व्यवधान) फाइनली मैं यह कहना चाहूंगा कि जो स्मॉल फाइनेंशियल बैंक्स हैं, उनका एक बहुत बड़ा रोल हमारे लद्यु और मध्यम उद्योगों को मजबूत करने में प्ले होता है। हमारे देश में 1 करोड़ 7 हजार लद्यु और मध्यम उद्योग पंजीकृत हैं, यानी कि रजिस्टर्ड हैं। इनमें से 90 परसेंट लद्यु यानी माइक्रो इंडस्ट्रीज हैं, जो ज्यादा से ज्यादा नौकरियां देने का काम करती हैं, लेकिन उनको लोन मिलने में बड़ी दिक्कत होती है।

महोदय, उन्हें लोन मिलने में बहुत दिक्कत होती है और यह प्रत्यक्ष रूप से मेरे संसदीय क्षेत्र अम्बेडकर में देखने को मिलता है। मेरी फाइनेंस मिनिस्ट्री से रिक्वेस्ट है कि नौकरी के मुद्‌दे पर अपना स्पष्टीकरण दे। इसके अलावा जो लघु और मध्यम उद्योग हैं, उन्हें उचित समय पर सस्ता ऋण दिलाने के लिए क्या आरबीआई से बातचीत करके उनकी क्रेडिट हिस्ट्री को बनाया जाता है जिससे कि उनकी निजता का ध्यान रखते हुए उनका फोन डेटा वगैरह लेकर ऐसा आंकड़ा निकल कर आए जिससे उन्हें आसानी से ऋण मिल सके? इसके लिए फाइनेंस मिनिस्ट्री क्या करेगी, इस पर भी मैं अपना प्रश्न रखता हूं।

DR. AMAR SINGH (FATEHGARH SAHIB): Thank you, hon. Chairperson Sir, for giving me this opportunity. I am really grateful to you for this.

Sir, the hon. Finance Minister is here. So, with your permission, through you, I want to ask one or two queries from her. The Supplementary Demands are described in the Constitution under Article 115. There are six parameters. I hope, you must have looked into those parameters and also followed them. I just want to be assured that yes, you have followed them. Otherwise, I feel, those conditions are quite tough. 

The second question which I want to ask is this. The amount of Rs. 4,35,938 crore is very big. Why is such a big amount, out of which Rs. 3,25,000 crore is for meeting revenue expenditure, being sought now? Was there no planning? These programmes relating to MGNREGA, fertilizer subsidy, and food subsidy are very well-known programmes. Every year, the amount of subsidy is going up. But what has happened now? Why was there a gap in the planning?

Hon. Chairperson Sir, the third question I want to ask the hon. Finance Minister, through you, is this. What would be the impact on fiscal deficit? The amount of Rs. 4,35,000 crore is very big. What would be its impact, and what steps the Government is taking to ensure that there is no inflation?

I have gone through your Budget document in which you have given very less information. For example, you are giving a sum of about Rs. 18,100 crore to BSNL in respect of viability gap funding. But you have given very less information. You have given the information like it is a one-time grant and also the steps being taken so that it is given again and again. I mean to say that you have given very minimal information on all those aspects as far as the Budget document is concerned. I would request you to give a little more information on it. 

Now, I come to these three main subsidies relating to food, MGNREGA, and fertilizer. All of us know about the MGNREGA. In the main Budget, you had cut the allocation for MGNREGA. In 2021, when it was proposed to be more than 1,00,000 crore, you had cut the allocation to only Rs. 73,000 crore. But now, you are giving it. What has happened in the country? मैं आपको अपने संसदीय क्षेत्र के बारे में बता सकता हूं कि 50 परसेंट यूटीलाइजेशन हुआ है। मजदूर हमें रोज घेरते हैं कि मजदूरी नहीं मिल रही है और हम सैक्रेटरी से पूछते हैं तो वह कहता है कि पैसा नहीं है। 

So, this reduction in allocation has really pinched the poor people in the country. Anyway, you are now giving a good amount towards it. But next year, we should not try to reduce the allocation. 

As regards food, there are two-three issues which I would like to flag before the Government of India. At the moment, the Central food stock of wheat is just above the buffer stock. Every month, about 25 to 30 lakh metric tonnes of wheat is being issued under two programmes, they are: NFSA and PMGKAY. About six months are there for the wheat to come because it comes only once. What are you going to do about it? There would be so much of inflation and so much of price rise of wheat. The Central stock is the indication for the whole country to keep the prices under control. So, I would like to know what steps you are taking in this regard. On the food issue alone, about Rs.3,000-4,000 crore is kept pending for Punjab. I will request that those monies be released. 

I have one or two suggestions. You are not going to take use of the 2021 Census. But you are using the 2011 Census for the ration card purpose. At least, you calculate something and extrapolate the number of people. About 10 crore poor people are being left out of the Public Distribution System. Please include them. 

Sir, I have only two issues to make regarding my constituency, and then I will conclude. 

I have been raising this one issue, and the hon. Minister of Civil Aviation has also assured me. The proposed Halwara International Airport falls in my constituency. It has been sanctioned under the UDAN Scheme. Rs.50 crore is required for the building. I will request you to please allot it so that the work starts. 

The second thing is, my constituency has a National Highway. The National Highway from Ambala to Rajpura and up to Ludhiana is in my constituency. There are so many accidents taking place on this National Highway. I want one medical college and one trauma centre on that road. I will be very happy if you do it. Thank you, Sir. 

SHRI K. NAVASKANI (RAMANATHAPURAM): Hon Chairman Sir, Vanakkam. Thank you for this opportunity to speak on the Supplementary Demands for Grants.

An amount of Rs. 5 crore is given as MPLAD fund every year. Keeping in view the price rise, increase in wages of workers, and the increase in the work estimate, this amount of Rs. 5 crore should be enhanced. 

In Tamil Nadu every Parliamentary Constituency has six Assembly Constituencies and each MLA gets Rs 3 crore as MLA Local Area development Fund. In view of this, Rs.5 crore earmarked as MPLAD fund is insufficient. We find difficulty in fulfilling the demands of the people with this Rs 5 crore fund every year. Therefore this amount should be enhanced.

Fishermen live in large numbers in my Ramanathapuram constituency. Time and again these Tamil fishermen are attacked by Sri Lankan Navy and their fishing boats are taken away by the Navy personnel of the neighbouring country. I urge that deep sea fishing should be encouraged by the Union Government as a solution to address these issues.

For deep sea fishing 80 per cent grant is given besides 10 percent loan from banks. Fishermen do not come forward to purchase boats through this Scheme as the grant is only for purchasing boats. They need to spend another 40 to 50 lakh rupees for purchasing nets and other fishing equipment. If this amount is included in the 80 per cent grant, then fishermen may come forward to purchase boats under this Scheme.

Scholarships given to the minority students through Dr Maulana Azad Foundation have been completely stopped. Pre-matric scholarships were provided to the minority students from Classes I to VIII. This has been withheld now. Citing free and compulsory education being provided upto 8th Class under Right to Education Act, 2009 as the reason, this Government has stopped giving these scholarships meant for minority students. The Minority Affairs Department should reconsider this decision and those scholarships have to be provided again to the minority students studying in Classes I to VIII.

In order to provide equal opportunity for getting education and for upholding social justice there is a need to provide these scholarships to them as it is the duty of this Government. The Report of Justice Sachar clearly explains how far these minority students are backward – socially, economically, and in getting employment. Stopping issue of scholarships given to minority students is injustice for them. Therefore, I urge that this Government should reconsider and provide again the scholarships to minority students.

As compared to last year’s Rs. 5029 crore allocation for minority welfare has been reduced to Rs 4510 crore this year, out of which there is a 6 per cent reduction as regards educational scholarships. Funds allocated during last year for education are less and that too remained unspent, as a result of which education of minority students is affected. This amount which is stopped should be released soon in order to ensure the welfare of minority students.

The financial help from Prime Minister’s National Relief Fund is not properly or completely released to the hospitals. All our recommendations are not being accepted by the hospitals as the financial help to be provided under this Scheme is kept pending for long.

Moreover, if they apply for Rs 8 lakh or Rs 10 lakh, they say that only a paltry sum of Rs 2 lakh to 3 lakh is received by them. I urge that the financial help provided under this Scheme to the poor people, should be enhanced and the payment pending for release to these hospitals should be expedited. 

DR. DNV SENTHILKUMAR S. (DHARMAPURI): Thank you, hon. Chairperson, Sir. I would like to emphasise on three major failures in the financial sector. The first is the demonetization. I do not want to go into the lines 'burn me alive if I don't deliver'. I just want to concentrate on what affects the common man. 

Sir, when demonetization was introduced, it was said that it was to do away with the black money. Of course, there is a simple logic – higher the denomination, it is much easier for the black money hoarders to hoard money. There was a technical glitch, and these ATMs were not working for almost a week. The main issue of demonetization at that time was that of Rs.2000 currency note. 

I would like to know one thing from the Finance Minister. Is it not true that not one ATM in India today delivers Rs.2000 currency note? Is it not true that not even one bank gives away, when you withdraw cash, Rs.2000 currency note? Is it an internal circular to collect all Rs.2000 notes and get them converted into Rs.500 notes? I want to have a clarification from the Finance Minster in this regard. So, this is the one big major failure in the financial sector.

Secondly, there are about 16 people who have defaulted with an amount of Rs.2.4 lakh crore. These 16 people are not the common men. These people just belong to the BJP ruled States. Is it not the duty of the Government to go and collect money from these defaulters. It is not a problem of the common man. 

The third point is with regard to the Swachch Bharat Mission. I would like the Government to conduct an audit of it. The intention of the Government with regard to constructing toilets through Swachch Bharat Mission was good. It was a very, very welcome scheme to eradicate open defecation from the country. But the amount of Rs.10,000 or Rs.12,000, which was sponsored both by the Union Government as well as the State Government, was very small. I would like to reiterate that an amount of Rs.12,000 is not at all enough to construct a functional toilet. 

Sir, I take it as a challenge. I will give you Rs.12,000. You send me anybody from the Ministry of Finance and show me how a functional toilet can be built with this amount. What I mean to say is that 10.9 crore people have constructed toilets. 

In Tamil Nadu alone about 55 lakh people have constructed toilets. The amount spent in constructing toilets in Tamil Nadu is about Rs.66,000 crore, and throughout India for that matter is about Rs.1,30,800 crore. This money has not just gone into the drain but has gone into the sewage. 

Madam, I would again say that it is a very good scheme. In the first phase of the scheme, we do not know whether this is a successful scheme or a failure. I would request the hon. Finance Minster to increase the grant for constructing toilets under Swachch Bharat Mission so that they are actually useful for the common man. 

I would urge the Government to approach the common man not with arrogance but grace. Thank you, Sir, for giving me this opportunity.

SHRI ADHIR RANJAN CHOWDHURY (BAHARAMPUR): Sir, I rise to dwell on the Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2022-23. The First Batch of the Supplementary Demands for Grants for 2022-23 includes 75 grants and 6 appropriations. 

Sir, approval of the Parliament is sought for gross additional expenditure of Rs.4,35,938.87 crore. The net cash outgo is estimated to be Rs.3,25,756.69 crore as additional expenditure is matched by savings or by enhanced receipts/ recoveries which is about Rs.1,10,180.59 crore. The token provision for reappropriation of savings is Rs.159 lakh. 

In the original Budget 2022-23, expenditure allocation was Rs.39,44,909 crore, and additional net expenditure allocation was Rs.3,25,756.69 crore. The total revised budget allocation now is Rs. 42,70,665.69 crore. In so far as ‘chemicals and fertilisers’ is concerned, the original grant in the Budget 2022-23 was Rs. 1,09,242.23 crore. Now, the total of original grant plus supplementary comes to Rs. 2,18,531.18 crore. The revised estimate in Budget 2021-22 was of Rs. 141,735 crore. Despite announcing an additional subsidy of Rs. 14,775 crore in May, 2021 and Rs. 6,553 crore in October, 2021 for non-urea fertilisers, experts had predicted a shortfall of Rs. 30,000 crore with urea shortage being the most dominant. 

Sir, the fact is that we are focussing only on urea and DAP, but other fertilisers should also be given due priority because experts always opine that the balanced application of fertilisers will yield more crop. So, I would request the hon. Minister to ponder over this issue. The rise of fertiliser prices has certainly increased the input costs, affecting the income of farmers which has been declining under this Government. As per the NSO-SAS survey 2021, real income from cultivation increased by 8.9 per cent between 2012-13 and 2018-19.

Again, in so far as ‘food and public distribution’ is concerned, the original grant in Budget 2022-23 was Rs. 2,25,959.58 crore. Now, the Supplementary DFG is of Rs. 80,348.31 crore. Now, the total of original grant plus supplementary comes to Rs. 3,06,307.89 crore. The revised estimate in Budget 2021-22 was of Rs. 3,02,000 crore. 

In this regard, I would like to know from the hon. Minister whether the Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Yojana will be extended beyond December because they are well aware that the purchasing power of the common people has not improved in spite of all the measures being taken by this Government. So, in view of the declining purchasing power of the poor people across the country, this programme could be extended. I do not know what the plan of this Government is, but I must propose the extension of this programme beyond December. 

Secondly, the National Food Security Act, 2013 requires that the subsidy covers 75 per cent of the rural population and 50 per cent of the urban population. At present, 81 crore persons are covered under the Act. 

Sir, in so far as ‘rural development’ aspect is concerned, the original grant in Budget 2022-23 was Rs. 1,35,944.29 crore and the Supplementary DFG is of Rs. 45,174.47 crore. Now, the total of original grant plus supplementary comes to Rs. 1,81,118.76 crore.

Sir, I do not want to harp on the issues being raised by my esteemed colleagues who spoke before me, but in this regard, I would like to simply draw the attention of the hon. Minister to the fact that the allocation for MGNREGS is Rs. 73,000 crore, which is 35 per cent lower than the last year’s revised estimates, which includes Rs. 40,000 crore of PMKSY fund. 

मैडम, सदन के अंदर सत्ता पक्ष के नुमाइंदे कहते हैं कि मनरेगा को बंद करना चाहिए। हमारे प्रधान मंत्री जी कहते हैं कि यह कांग्रेस और यूपीए के जमाने की नाकामी की धरोहर है और इस धरोहर को बचाये रखना चाहिए। जब कोविड आया था तो बड़े जोर-शोर से यह कहा गया था कि कोविड के समय आम लोगों को बुरी हालत से बचाने के लिए मैंने मनरेगा में बहुत सारा पैसा दिया। सरकार के एक-एक रुख और एक-एक रवैये में ऐसा क्यों होता है? सरकार की तरफ से जो मंत्री या नुमाइंदे हैं, वे एक स्वर में मनरेगा के लाभ के बारे में स्पष्टीकरण क्यों नहीं देते हैं? मेरा यह एक महत्वपूर्ण सवाल है।

Insofar as revenue is concerned, original grant in budget 2022-23 was Rs. 2,27,552.52 crore and Supplementary Demands for Grants is Rs. 19,728.49 crore. The total amount comes to Rs. 2,47,281.01 crore. In June 2020, reports indicated that the Central Government informed the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Finance that it did not have the funds required to honour its statutory commitment to States to provide them GST compensation. 

Even the Attorney General, K.K. Venugopal reportedly opined that the Central Government was not obligated to pay the GST compensation shortfall and that States should borrow from the market against future compensation receipts.

During the 47th GST Council meet, held on June 29, 2022, the Government decided to hike GST rates for essential items, effective from July 18, 2022. This move has been met with much contention owing to already increasing prices of essential items and uncontrollable inflation. The Union Finance Minister, Mrs. Sitharaman insisted that this GST hike was decided upon only after approval from all States. That claim has been denied by the Finance Ministers of the respective States.

You are in your own way imposing cesses and surcharges. On the other hand, you are not meeting the promises that you have given on the floor of the House to those individual States. So, certainly, sometimes it is appearing that you are breaching your commitment made regarding legal mechanisms to the State Governments across the country.

I would like to flag the attention of the House to this point. So far as fiscal deficit is concerned, India’s tax revenue collections are likely to be higher than budget estimate by Rs. 2-2.5 lakh crore. In spite of that, the fiscal deficit is likely to overshoot the Government’s target of 6.4 per cent of GDP by Rs. 0.8-1 lakh crore. You are in a position to elucidate on this aspect. But what has been observed by us is that you yourself are giving a triple warning, that is, current account deficit; fiscal deficit; and States’ deficit. I do not know how you will be reconciling the fiscal deficit with the growth of the economy as has been committed by this Government. Secondly, the Supplementary Demands for Grants of this scale indicate a gross miscalculation on the part of the Government on expected expenditure. It also undermines parliamentary control by going above and beyond what had initially been sanctioned.

Insofar as fertilizers is concerned, I have already indicated that the NPK ratio refers to the proportion of volume of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium in fertilizers. The ideal average NPK ratio is 4:2:1. But the ratio increased to 7.7:3.1:1 in 2021-22. The ratio was 6.8:2.7:1 during Kharif 2021, which got further distorted to 12.8:5.1:1 during Kharif 2022. 

While farmers tend to use fertilizers in a balanced ratio, changes in prices due to policy changes end up upsetting the balance. So, there may be distortion of the balance that I have flagged your attention to.

As far as fertilizers’ shortage is concerned, the Indian Government insists that there is no fertilizer shortage in the country and there is sufficient stock to fulfil existing demand. Yet, farmers across the country have been facing shortages of fertilizers for both Rabi and Kharif sowing seasons, including Rajasthan – the State from which Arjun Ram Meghwal ji comes – Himachal Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Odisha, and Tamil Nadu. The increase in fertilizer prices was partly responsible for a 27 per cent drop in paddy sowing during Kharif this year. The Government is meanwhile on the path to disinvesting or shutting down every PSU in the fertilizer sector. On the other hand, the import of DAP and NP/NPK complex fertilizers increased year-on-year by 45.2 per cent and 76.1 per cent respectively in April-October 2022.

There is a slogan being propagated, `One Nation, One Fertiliser’, which was launched in September 2022. But that goes against Standing Committee’s recommendations. The Committee remarked that the farmers should have the choice to buy fertilisers from different brands. The only way to ensure efficient use of subsidy is by directing it to the farmer's account. However, under the `One Nation, One Fertiliser’ Scheme, all fertilisers are supposed to be sold under the Bharat brand name. This will lead to lower margins for manufacturers and leave them with no incentive to increase production of quality fertilisers. In order to increase their brand loyalty, the manufacturers will now need to focus on marketing processes, instead of focusing attention on upgrading systems.

There is another issue. There is no update to the list of beneficiaries under the National Food Security Act (NFSA). Section 9 of the National Food Security Act, 2013 requires that the list of beneficiaries be updated on the basis of the latest Census data. With the delay in the 2021 Census, the list of beneficiaries under the Scheme is outdated by 11 years. If the list of beneficiaries were to be adjusted as per the directives of the Supreme Court, there would be an increase of 10 crore beneficiaries under the Scheme. So, I think the Government should take into account the concerns of the people and also the observations made by the hon. Supreme Court.

Madam, what is very intriguing to me and what is concerning to all the sections of our population is that the Reserve Bank of India increased the repo rate for the fifth time in Financial Year 2023 in an attempt to tackle inflation. To tackle inflation, you are resorting to increase in repo rate. Why? Why is this kind of mechanism being adopted by you? On 7th December, 2022, the RBI increased its monetary repo rate to 6.25 per cent, a 35 basis point hike from 5.90 per cent. The repo or policy rate is at its highest level since August 2018 The six-member Monetary Policy Committee arrived at this calculation after an assessment of the evolving macroeconomic situation unfolding in the country. Annual rate of wholesale inflation was at 12.41 per cent in August 2022 and 10.7 per cent in September 2022. 

Compared to it, it is at a 30-year high of 15.08 per cent in April, 2022. While this may be a relief to many, States like Kerala are still reeling from the effects of price rise. Retail inflation in India in September, 2022 hit a five-month high at 7.41 per cent. The figure crossed the Reserve Bank of India’s upper limit of 6 per cent for the ninth month. Inflation in October, 2022 is still above the RBI’s limit of 6.77 per cent. The headline inflation is forecasted to be 6.4 per cent in 2022-2023. Why is it so? The inflation rate has peaked, and the Indian economy is expected to take 2-3 years to return to an inflation rate of 4 per cent. This implies that the RBI will continue to maintain higher interest rates over the next five years, which are critical in kick-starting economic growth required to move away from the pandemic slump.

Already, the media people have been highlighting that industrial output as measured by the Index of Industrial Production slumps to a 26-month low of -4 per cent in October due to contraction in manufacturing and consumer goods. According to the NSO data, it is indicating weak exports and sluggish consumption demand alongside the continuing weakness for small and medium enterprises. We are eager to know why the Central Bank would not keep inflation within the targeted 6 per cent upper limit for the three consecutive quarters.

Why does the Government not take efforts to develop the Eastern Region vis-à-vis our State of West Bengal as a priority sector? West Bengal should not be made a target because we are in power. We are for the interest of the country. We want to stand by the Government. But at every step and every moment, if attempts are made to create economic blockade of the whole State, it is not tolerable. 

So, our allegation is that the Government of India is trying to create economic blockade of the State of West Bengal and from that they should withdraw their vision and withdraw their ideas. Let them extend the hands of cooperation. The letters which I have mentioned here, I will hand them over to the hon. Finance Minister by which she can have a look and can send a reply. There is nothing wrong in this… (Interruptions)

माननीय अध्यक्ष : निशिकांत जी आप क्या बोल रहे थे?

डॉ. निशिकांत दुबे : अध्यक्ष महोदय, सुदीप बाबू सीनियर लीडर हैं। रूल-349, 352 और 353, इन्होंने तीनों रूल का वॉयलेशन किया है। जे.पी.नड्डा साहब दूसरे हाउस के सदस्य हैं और भारतीय जनता पार्टी के राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष हैं। उन्होंने कोलकाता में क्या भाषण दिया, आप बाहर के भाषण को कोट नहीं कर सकते हैं। वे दूसरे सदन के सदस्य हैं। आप बिना नोटिस के उनको कोट नहीं कर सकते हैं।

दूसरा, वे भारतीय जनता पार्टी के राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष हैं। कौल और शकधर कहता है कि यदि पार्टी के अध्यक्ष के ऊपर या पार्टी के ऊपर एलिगेशन करते हैं तो आपको नोटिस देना होगा। यदि कोई दूसरे सदन का सदस्य है और आप उनका नाम कोट करना चाहते हैं तो आपको नोटिस देना होगा और सदन के बाहर क्या हुआ है, उसको आप कोट नहीं कर सकते हैं। ये तीनों रूल का वॉयलेशन हुआ है 

मेरी आपसे रिक्वेस्ट है कि जे.पी.नड्डा और भारतीय जनता पार्टी का जो भी रेफरेंस आया है, उसको डिलीट कर दीजिए। … (व्यवधान)

माननीय अध्यक्ष : मैं इसको देखता हूं।

SHRI SUDIP BANDYOPADHYAY: Sir, I am reading a letter only. It is a letter … (Interruptions)

माननीय अध्यक्ष : माननीय सदस्य, आप एक वरिष्ठ सदस्य हैं। माननीय प्रधान मंत्री जी और मुख्य मंत्री जी के पत्राचार को सप्लीमेंट्री बजट में टेबल नहीं कर सकते हैं। 

श्री सुदीप बन्दोपाध्याय : अध्यक्ष महोदय, हम मिनिस्टर को तो दे सकते हैं?

माननीय अध्यक्ष : आप मिनिस्टर को चैम्बर में जाकर दे सकते हैं। 

SHRI SUDIP BANDYOPADHYAY: I can hand it over to the Minister … (Interruptions)

श्री अधीर रंजन चौधरी : महोदय, आप कुछ बोलना चाहते थे, क्या मैं बोल दूं?...(व्यवधान) एक बात है, बंगाल में जो कटाव हो रहा है, सरकार उस कटाव को थोड़ा देखे, क्योंकि गांव, जमीन, जायदाद, मंदिर और मस्जिद तबाह होते जा रहे हैं। सालों से ऐसा हो रहा है। मुर्शिदाबाद, मालदा तबाह हो रहे हैं।…(व्यवधान) बंगाल की सरकार कहती है कि केन्द्र पैसा नहीं देती है।….(व्यवधान) केन्द्र सरकार कहती है कि राज्य सरकार पैसा देगी।…(व्यवधान) हम बीच में फंसे हुए हैं। सूबे की सरकार भी नहीं देखती है और केन्द्र सरकार भी नहीं देखती है। हम बीच में फंसे हुए हैं।…(व्यवधान)

SHRI MARGANI BHARAT (RAJAHMUNDRY): Thank you, Speaker, Sir. I take this opportunity to speak about the interest of the people of the State of Andhra Pradesh.

माननीय अध्यक्ष : आपको बोलने के लिए दो मिनट का समय दिया गया है।

… (व्यवधान)

SHRI MARGANI BHARAT: Sir, the House, rather the whole country, must be knowing about the State of Andhra Pradesh. The State was unscientifically bifurcated during the UPA tenure. The hon. Prime Minister made a promise that Andhra Pradesh will be given Special Category Status but due to some unavoidable reasons of the 14th Finance Commission, the Special Category Status was denied to the State. At a later stage, the 15th Finance Commission mentioned that the Union Government can take an appropriate decision.

माननीय अध्यक्ष : इस विषय पर किसने वादा किया था? आप ये विषय हमेशा उठाते रहते हैं। इसका विषय बताइएगा।

… (व्यवधान)

SHRI MARGANI BHARAT: Sir, I am speaking on the Supplementary Demands for Grants. We need grants for the State of Andhra Pradesh. Once the State got unscientifically bifurcated, if any issue is raised it should not be considered as the voice of Andhra Pradesh but the voice of the country. Our hon. Chief Minister, Shri Jagan Mohan Reddy has met the Prime Minister and all the Union Ministers a number of times and has requested them to give a special grant to the State of Andhra Pradesh. Sir, we are like a small baby. We are malnourished. The people of Andhra Pradesh should not think that they are in minority. We are 25 in number. Injustice is being meted out to the State of Andhra Pradesh. The Government of India should show magnanimity and sanction grants to the State of Andhra Pradesh. Take for example, two brothers are separated, and one brother is given huge wealth and the other is given nothing. The Government of India, playing the role of father, has to do justice.

माननीय अध्यक्ष : संसदीय कार्य मंत्री जी, यह बंटवारा कब हुआ था? 

… (व्यवधान)

संसदीय कार्य मंत्री; कोयला मंत्री तथा खान मंत्री (श्री प्रहलाद जोशी) : महोदय, वर्ष 2014 में हुआ था ।…(व्यवधान)

SHRI MARGANI BHARAT: Already nine years have passed but till now nothing has happened. The then Minister, Shri Venkaiah Naidu mentioned in the House itself that the State of Andhra Pradesh shall be given Special Category Status for ten years.

माननीय अध्यक्ष : अगर आप किसी का नाम लेंगे, तो निशिकांत जी आपको नियम के बारे में बता देंगे। 

… (व्यवधान)

SHRI MARGANI BHARAT: Sir, he said this in this House, and not in the other House.

डॉ. निशिकांत दुबे : महोदय, जब वर्ष 2014 में ये बंटवारा हुआ था, तब वेंकैया जी इस सदन के सदस्य नहीं थे। उन्होंने राज्य सभा में क्या कहा, क्या नहीं कहा, ये यहां डिस्कस नहीं हो सकता है। He was not a Minister at that time. He was not a Member of the Lok Sabha.

SHRI MARGANI BHARAT: He mentioned it in Lok Sabha. And also, the then Prime Minister … (Interruptions)

PROF. SOUGATA RAY: Dr. Manmohan Singh was the Prime Minister at that time. He assured the House at the time of the division of the State that Andhra Pradesh will be given Special Category Status. 

SHRI MARGANI BHARAT: That too not for five years but for ten years. We were seeking different ways like the Private Members’ Bill, A. P. Reorganisation Bill of 2022, in which we wanted to include the special category status. Why such kind of a situation has arisen?

One of the TDP Members is… * I would like to refer Bihar. We are not that poor to pay salaries. We have enough to pay salaries. The Minister of Finance has informed the State that Rs.17,923 crore cut is being imposed on the current borrowing due to over borrowings by the TDP Government during the 14th Finance Commission. That has been adjusted in what the Central Government is now giving to the State. During the TDP tenure all the mistakes were committed, and because of that the funds given to the State have been reduced. If any action has to be taken by the Central Government, they should take against the previous Government. The Central Government should take care of the grant that should come to the State.

Polavaram Project is the lifeline of the State of Andhra Pradesh. Once Hyderabad, the Capital city, is given to Telangana, the funds meant for the Polavaram Project should be given to the State of Andhra Pradesh.

It has happened for the first time in the history of our country. The State Government is investing money for a national project and the Central Government is reimbursing money. How is it possible? More than Rs. 2,800 crore are yet to be reimbursed by the Centre. I would like to request the Central Government to release funds at the earliest. 

Hon. Speaker, Sir, the State of Andhra Pradesh is having the longest coastline after Gujarat. Our hon. Chief Minister is going ahead to build fishing harbours. We request that funds be provided to the State of Andhra Pradesh. 

Hon. Speaker, Sir, through you, I would like to request the hon. Finance Minister to nurture the State of Andhra Pradesh.

Thank you, Sir.

SHRI RAVNEET SINGH (LUDHIANA): I thank you, Hon’ble Speaker sir, for giving me the opportunity to speak on the Supplementary Demands for Grant. Almost all points have been raised by members in the House. I am happy to note that India has surpassed Britain financially. The British P.M is of India origin. It is a happy news. Our economy today is thriving. It is good. But, we must give credit to the earlier Congress governments for laying the foundation stone of our economy. One should talk about that also. Economy is a continuous process.

As far as schemes are concerned, whether it is Swachh Bharat, MNREGA, or Jan- Dhan scheme, they must be implemented properly. About 20 to 30 schemes are there, which were there earlier too. Their names were changed to make them sound like new schemes. I have a long list of changed names.

Sir, why this Supplementary demand for Grants was needed 7 let me also say that out festivals play a pivotal role in giving a boost to our economy. Our festivals are celebrated throughout the year. People spend money during festivals very liberally. This helps the economy. The tent walllahs, fruit vendors, vegetable vendors, all gain out of it. Hotel industry thrives and it infuses our economy with positivity. 

Our old ladies used to save money at home. They had money-pots where they kept money as savings. These small things too give a boost to economy.

We are at 103rd place in Global Hunger Index. We are at 168th place in literacy rate. World Happiness index finds us at 133rd place. We are at 125th place in Gender discrimination. Financial Development Index finds us at 51st spot. We are at 180th place in Environment performance Index. These are negative situations we must look into.

We say, our economy has ample money. But 100 people have got 800 million with them. Common man is in a miserable condition. In towns and cities, there is no work left. Poor people are returning to rural areas for doing work in MNREGA. Bandopadhyay ji has rightly said that the condition today is dismal.

Rs. 1.10 lakh crore in this budget is being given as fertilizer subsidy. More goods trains should be sent to Punjab with fertilizers.

Sir, I was surprised to note that Rs. 2000/- is being given under Kisan Nidhi Scheme. 11.84 lakh farmers got the first instalment. But, the 11th instalment has been given to only 3.84 lakh farmers. This is a matter of concern. In Punjab 51.54% drop is there in this scheme. Very less beneficiaries have got the money in the 11th instalment.

Sir, I hail from Punjab. 80,000 crores more additional expenditure has been asked for. It is needed for P.M. Garib Kalyan Yojana. Crores of people are benefitting. But the FCI report says that earlier, we had 90.81. million metric tonnes as buffer stock. What is worrying is that now it is only 60.11 million metric tonnes. Will we be able to give this food grain to our people only during elections? Or we will be able to feed one and all?

Sir, I hail from Ludhiana. Due to Russia- Ukraine war, our hosiery industry has suffered a lot. Post- Covid, these has been a 20% to 30% decrease in purchase of hosiery items by people. Some special package to this industry should be announced by the finance Minister. Our bicycle industry has been demanding that their GST be reduced from 12% to 5%, It pertains to poor people.

The Central –State Combined Interest- among G-20 countries is 9.2% which is highest. When Vajpayee ji was the P.M we had said that it should not go above 3% to 4%. How much money will we borrow? 

My last point, Sir, is this. IMF and World Bank are saying that the next year may see recession setting in. Hon’ble Finance Minister may look into this seriously. 

Thank you.

Title: Business of the House (The Speaker made an Observation regarding converting Calling attention to short Duration Discussion under Rule 193 considering importance of subject regarding Problem of Drug Abuse in the country and steps taken by Government thereon.).

माननीय अध्यक्ष : माननीय सदस्यगण, देश में मादक द्रव्यों के सेवन की समस्या और इस संबंध में सरकार द्वारा उठाए गए कदमों के बारे में चर्चा में श्रीमती हरसिमरत कौर बादल, श्री पी.वी. मिधुन रेड्डी, श्री गुरजीत सिंह औजला के नाम से ध्यानाकर्षण प्रस्ताव सूचीबद्ध है । विषय के महत्व को देखते हुए और कुछ माननीय सदस्यों ने इस पर बोलने की इच्छा प्रकट की है, उनका सुझाव था कि ध्यानाकर्षण प्रस्ताव के प्रारूप में ऐसा संभव नहीं है इसलिए मैं सदन की सहमति से सूचीबद्ध इस चर्चा को नियम 193 के अधीन चर्चा में परिवर्तित कर रहा हूँ, ताकि अधिकाधिक सदस्यों को इसमें भाग लेने का अवसर मिले । मुझे आशा है कि इस पर सदन की सहमति होगी और एक सार्थक चर्चा होगी । यह लंच के बाद लिया जाएगा ।

अनेक माननीय सदस्य: जी हाँ ।

Title: Regarding attempt to change and distort Indian history.

PROF. SOUGATA RAY (DUM DUM): Sir, I rise to speak on a matter of public importance. In recent times, there has been an effort by the Government and the Ruling Party at the Centre to change and distort the history of the country. The Home Minister has said that history should be written anew and he is referring to the Mughal age. He says that the Mughals had invaded forgetting that Mughals gave a stable Government to India for 200 years. The Taj Mahal, the Red Fort and the Jama Masjid were all constructed during their times. 

Sir, we strongly believe that the culture of India is not a Hindu culture, it is a composite culture. We also strongly believe that this should not be a Hindu history or a Muslim history or a British history. There should be an Indian history. But this distortion of history is not only in the change of names of cites. Allahabad suddenly becomes Prayagraj. Aurangabad suddenly becomes Sambhajinagar. This is re-writing history. It was done in Communist people’s time. The most important thing has to be mentioned and that is to write the history of Indian freedom struggle properly during the Amrit Kaal of our Independence. We should write clearly that ...* asked for clemency from the British. … (Interruptions) I have given a notice and I am speaking accordingly..… (Interruptions) Sir, it should be mentioned that ...* refused to participate in the Quit India Movement of 1942.

डॉ. निशिकांत दुबे (गोड्डा) : कहां लिखा हुआ है?

PROF. SOUGATA RAY: It is written in every place. There is constant effort to distort the history of India and make us forget that the Hindutva walas did not participate in the freedom struggle and belittle Jawaharlal Nehru’s contribution. Jawaharlal Nehru spent nine years in British jail. None of these Hindutva walas including ... * did spend time.… (Interruptions)

माननीय अध्यक्ष : इनके पुराने नेता हैं, यह उनका संदर्भ है।

डॉ. निशिकांत दुबे : कहां लिखा हुआ है?

PROF. SOUGATA RAY: ...* positively refused to participate…… (Interruptions) I will bring ten books.… (Interruptions)

HEENA VIJAYKUMAR GAVIT (NANDURBAR): Several provisions have been incorporated in the Constitution for safeguarding and promoting the interests and rights of the Scheduled Tribes in various spheres so as to enable them to join the national mainstream. Article 46, Article 275, Articles 335 and Articles 342 cast a duty on the State to promote with special care, the educational and economic interests of the Scheduled Tribes. The Government of India is taking several steps to promote the welfare of Students belonging to scheduled, tribe community through scholarship. However, the actual objective of these schemes to uplift the marginalized is defeated due to the presence of an income criteria of the family. In Pre Matric and Post Matric Scholarship Scheme for ST students the family income limit is 2,50,000 per annum and for National Overseas Scholarship for ST students for studying abroad and National Scholarship Scheme, it is 6 lakh per annum. Title: Regarding appointment of security guards in ATM booths of Banks- Laid.

Title : Regarding access of advanced medical technology for patients suffering from heart valve disease- Laid.  

DR. LORHO PFOZE (OUTER MANIPUR): A large population in India suffers from valvular heart disease. While degenerative heart valve diseases mainly affect older people, developing Countries witness the prevalence of rheumatic heart valve disease, affecting the younger population. 

Medical technologies to deliver better/safer patient outcomes are some developments over the past six decades. Pioneering work in heart valve replacement started in the early 1950s. Mechanical valves were introduced to replace the natural valves in the human heart and treat valvular heart disease. However, one of the inherent limitations of this technology included requiring patients to be on life-long blood thinners. 

A better solution was proposed in the 1970s with the development of biological tissue valves using either porcine (pig) or bovine (ox) pericardium, allowing patients to lead a better quality of life. However, tissue valves presented degeneration limitation and required repeat surgery. The newer tissue valves exhibit evidence of upto 30 years of longevity among patients over 60 years.

The most recent revolution is the advent of transcatheter valve replacement as an alternative to surgical intervention in severe aortic stenosis patients. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation does not require open-heart surgery.

I urge upon the Government to create an enabling environment to access advanced medical technology for all patients.

मैं सबसे पहले इस देश के यशस्वी प्रधान मंत्री श्री नरेन्द्र मोदी जी का अभिनन्दन करना चाहता हूं और उनका आभार व्यक्त करना चाहता हूं कि उन्होंने कई बार अपने ‘मन की बात’ कार्यक्रम में इस विषय के बारे में, नशाखोरी के बारे में इस देश की जनता को, विशेष रूप से युवाओं को चेताया और इससे बचने की अपील की ।

दूसरी बात, प्रधान मंत्री जी ने पहली बार देश के अंदर वर्ष 2018 में सामाजिक कल्याण और सशक्तिकरण मंत्रालय की ओर से बहुत ही व्यापक सर्वे करवाया, जिसका नाम “National Survey on Extent and Pattern of Substance Use in India” है । यह देश के सभी राज्यों में और सभी केंद्र शासित प्रदेशों में किया गया । एम्स, 10 मेडिकल कॉलेज, 15 एनजीओ और 1500 लोगों ने मिलकर इस सर्वे को किया । इस देश में किस प्रकार की एक राष्ट्रीय नीति और रणनीति बनायी जा सके, जिससे युवा शक्ति को हम कैसे बचा सकें । मैं आदरणीय प्रधान मंत्री का अभिनन्दन इसलिए भी करना चाहूंगा कि उनके प्रयास से पहली बार इन मादक पदार्थों के बारे में अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सहयोग के लिए 27 देशों के साथ द्विपक्षीय समझौते किए गए, 15 देशों के साथ एमओयू किया गया और दो देश, जर्मनी और सउदी अरब के साथ भी इसके बारे में समझौता किया गया ।

मैं इस देश के माननीय गृह मंत्री श्री अमित शाह जी का भी आभार व्यक्त करता हूं कि उन्होंने कुछ समय पूर्व उत्तर-पूर्व में बोलते हुए यह कहा था कि यह नशा, नारकोटिक्स हमारे युवाओं को दीमक की तरह खा रहा है । ड्रग एडिक्ट एक अपराध ही नहीं, बल्कि एक विक्टिम और भुक्तभोगी है । उन्होंने मादक पदार्थों के राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा के बारे में चंडीगढ़ के अंदर एक राष्ट्रीय सम्मेलन आयोजित किया और गुवाहाटी तथा गांधीनगर में दो क्षेत्रीय सम्मेलन भी किए । इसलिए मैं उनका भी धन्यवाद करता हूं ।

महोदय, मैं अपनी बात एक शास्त्रीय कथन से करना चाहता हूं:-

“अमन्त्रमक्षरं नास्ति नास्ति मूलमनौषधम् ।
 अयोग्यः पुरुषो नास्ति योजकस्तत्र दुर्लभः॥”

इस दुनिया के अंदर कोई भी ऐसा पदार्थ नहीं है, जो बिल्कुल बेकार हो, बिल्कुल यूजलेस हो । चाहे वह अफीम हो, चाहे वह गांजा हो, चाहे वह भांग हो, इस दुनिया के अंदर हर एक पदार्थ का कुछ न कुछ उपयोग है । अगर हम यह कहें कि कोई चीज बेकार है, तो यह हमारी अज्ञानता  है । ठीक इसी तरह से भगवान और प्रकृति ने इस दुनिया में जो भी पदार्थ बनाए हैं, कहीं न कहीं उनका कुछ उपयोग है, कहीं न कहीं उनका मेडिसनल यूज है । 

ये बात भी पूर्ण सत्य नहीं है कि इस दुनिया में हमेशा से नशाखोरी और शराब थी । जो लोग शुरू से इसको पीते थे, दुर्भाग्य से इस प्रकार के कुछ लोग हैं, जो इस बात का दुष्प्रचार करने की कोशिश करते हैं । वे यह भी आक्षेप लगाते हैं कि हमारे ऋषि-मुनि भी शराब पीते थे । ये एकदम नितांत असत्य है । हमारे यहां इस प्रकार के काफी उदाहरण हैं । मैं आप लोगों और इस हाउस के समक्ष एक उदाहरण रखना चाहता हूं । 

उपनिषदों के अंदर एक कथा आती है । हमारे देश में एक राजा हुए थे । उनका नाम अश्वपति था । उनके यहां 9 ऋषिगण गए और राजा ने उनको अपने यहां इन्वाइट किया और कहा कि आप हमारे यहां आकर भोजन करिए । तब ऋषियों ने कहा कि पता नहीं राजा के यहां किस प्रकार का रेवेन्यू आता है, वह कैसे धन इकट्ठा करते हैं, हो सकता है कि वह पाप की कमाई हो, इसलिए हम आपके यहां भोजन नहीं करेंगे । तब राजा अश्वपति ने घोषणा की थी –

न मे स्तेनो जनपदे, न कदर्यो न मद्यपः ।

बहुत से लोग इस बात को जानते हैं कि जब अंग्रेजों ने इस देश पर राज किया, तब उन्होंने भारतवर्ष में अफीम की खेती शुरू की । अफीम की खेती शुरू करके, वे उसको चाइना भेजते थे और चाइना से सिल्क खरीदकर अपने देश ले जाते थे । जब मादक पदार्थों ने चीन की युवा शक्ति को बर्बाद करने का काम किया और जब चीन के राजा ने इस बात का विरोध किया, तो आप सब लोगों को मालूम है कि उस समय अंग्रेंजो ने किस प्रकार से चीन के साथ दो युद्ध किए । एक युद्ध सन् 1839 में और दूसरा युद्ध सन् 1860 में हुआ । उन्होंने अपने देश में भी इसको बढ़ाने की कोशिश की थी । चाहे शराब की बात हो, चाहे अफीम की खेती की बात हो । केवल एक अपवाद  है । मुझे लगता है कि हमारे कांग्रेस पार्टी के मित्रों को भी यह बात अच्छी लगेगी, ए. ओ. ह्यूम ने इंडियन नेशन कांग्रेस की स्थापना की थी । पट्टाभि सीतारमैया जी ने हिस्ट्री ऑफ द इंडियन नेशनल कांग्रेस नामक एक किताब लिखी है । उसके दो बड़े-बड़े और मोटे वैल्यूम हैं । इस देश के अंदर आबकारी कमिश्नर बने थे । 

उन्होंने सन् 1859 में लिखा था कि “While we debauch our subjects, we do not even pecuniarily derive any profit from their ruin.” अभी प्रोफेसर साहब बोल रहे थे । मैं आबकारी/शराब की बात कर रहा हूं । “Of this revenue, the wages of sin, it may in the words of the old adage be truly said that ill-gotten wealth never thrives, and for every rupee additional that the Abkari yields, two at least are lost to the public by crime, and spent by the Government in suppressing it. I, at this moment, see no hopes of reform. I have no doubt whatsoever that if I be spared a few years longer, I shall live to see effaced in a more Christian-like system one of the greatest existing blots on our Government of India.” ये उस समय ए. ओ. ह्यूम ने लिखा था ।

मुंबई और दिल्ली जैसे बड़े शहरों में इसका प्रभाव बढ़ता जा रहा है । नशाखोरी के जो नुकसान हैं, जिनको आज हम यहां डिसकस करना चाहते हैं, सब लोग इस बात को मानते हैं कि इसका स्वास्थ्य के ऊपर विपरीत परिणाम होता सुप्रीम कोर्ट का एक जजमेंट आया था कि हाइवेज की 100 मीटर दूरी तक शराब की दुकानें न खोली जाएं । इससे क्राइम बढ़ता है, मर्डर्स होते हैं । वर्ष 2013 में लंदन में एक कांफ्रेंस हुई थी – पोलिसिंग दि सिटिज । उसके अंदर कैनबरा के एक मेयर आए थे, उन्होंने वहां एक बात कही थी कि जो पब्स चलते हैं, जो बार चलते हैं, वहां पर रात एक बजे तक एल्कोहल और ड्रग्स बिकती हैं । उन्होंने कैनबरा शहर का उदाहरण दिया कि पहले वहां रात एक बजे तक जो पब्स चलते थे, उसको उन्होंने 11 बजे तक किया और 11 बजे तक करने के बाद वहां क्राइम में बहुत कमी आई और कानून-व्यवस्था बहुत अच्छी हो गई । उन्होंने कहा कि अगर मेरा वश चलेगा तो मैं इन पब्स और बार को बन्द करूंगा । इससे महिलाओं के साथ छेड़खानी के केसेज कम होते हैं, डोमेस्टिक वायलेंस में कमी आती है । अभी पंजाब और राजस्थान का जिक्र हो रहा था । पंजाब और राजस्थान में ड्रग्स का जो मेनेस बढ़ा है, हमारे दुश्मन देश को होने वाला है । जैसा मैंने पहले कहा था, ड्रग एडिक्शन की जब शुरुआत होती है, हम अपने स्कूल-कॉलेज और घरों में इसको पीयर प्रेशर और दोस्ती में शुरू करते हैं । किसी ने एक बहुत अच्छा शेर कहा है :

“खुश्क बातों में कहां है शेख़ कैफ-ए-जिन्दगी, 

वो तो पीकर ही मिलेगा जो मजा पीने में है ।”

नशे खाने में जो मजा है, वह मजा खाकर ही मालूम होगा, जब इस प्रकार की बातें की जाती हैं, तब यह प्रवृत्ति बढ़ती जाती है । हमारे स्कूलों और घरों में संस्कारों और नैतिक मूल्यों की शिक्षा जिस प्रकार से कमी हुई, उससे ड्रग एडिक्ट्स और मादक पदार्थों की समस्याएं बढ़ती जा रही हैं ।

ड्रग एडिक्ट के बारे में कुछ समस्याएं हैं और प्रैक्टिकल समस्याए हैं । जो लोग ड्रग खाते हैं, उनको पुलिस अरेस्ट करे तो उनको लेकर कहां जाएं? जब मैं मुंबई में पुलिस कमिश्नर था, वहां के कोर्ट मौखिक आदेश करते थे कि ड्रग एडिक्ट को पकड़कर मत लाइए, कोर्ट में इनका क्या करेंगे और जेल का प्रशासन उनको रखना नहीं चाहता है । इसी तरह से बिना ड्रग के उनको विदड्रॉल सिम्पटम्स आते हैं, उनको रखने के लिए कोई तैयार नहीं होता है । 

इस ड्रग एब्यूज का हल क्या होता है, जैसा मैंने पहले कहा था कि घर, स्कूल या कॉलेज में नैतिक शिक्षा दी जाए । मैं अपने आदरणीय प्रधान मंत्री मोदी जी का अभिनन्दन करना चाहूंगा कि वर्ष 2020 की हमारी जो राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति आई है, उस राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा नीति के अंदर पहली बार इस बात पर बहुत जोर दिया गया है कि हमारी एजुकेशन के अंदर मोरल एजुकेशन पर जोर दिया जाए, ताकि हमारे बच्चे सही रह सकें । हम इस मजे की संस्कृति में हेल्थ और हैप्पीनेस की तरफ जाएं ।

महोदय, मैं एक बात और कहना चाहूंगा । यहां पर हमारे आदरणीय गृह मंत्री जी बैठे हुए  हैं । एनडीपीएस एक्ट में पहले एक संशोधन किया गया था और वह संशोधन यह था कि अगर छोटी क्वांटिटी है तो उनको बेल हो जाती है, मगर कॉमर्शियल क्वांटिटी है तो उनको बेल नहीं होती है । इसमें यह हो जाता है कि हम छोटी चोरी को माफ कर दें और बड़ी चोरी माफ नहीं होती है । एक्सपीरियंस यह कहता है कि ये ड्रग रेकेटर्स कल को ट्रैफिकर बन जाते हैं । ये उसका व्यापार करने लगते हैं । इस वजह से मुझे लगता है कि इस पर पुनर्विचार करने की जरूरत है और योग, स्पोर्ट्स कल्चर को बढ़ावा देने की जरूरत है । 

महोदय, मैं एक निवेदन और करूंगा कि नशामुक्ति अभियान के तहत हमारे जितने सेंटर्स चलते हैं, चाहे इंटीग्रेटेड रिहैबिलिटेशन सेंटर्स हों, आउट रीच एंड ड्रॉप इन सेंटर्स हों, उनका रेगुलेशन और इंस्पेक्शन अच्छा किया जाए । मैं सरकार से एक निवेदन और करना चाहूंगा । मैं जब सीबीआई के अंदर था तो मैं एंटी नारकोटिक्स का चीफ था । मैं एक बार चित्तौड़गढ़ और मंदसौर जिले में भेष बदलकर घूम रहा था । यह बात आज भी है कि किसान वहां अफीम की खेती करते हैं और वहां पर अफीम का सरकारी रेट काफी कम है और ग्रे मार्केट के अंदर उसका 10-15 गुना रेट है । इसलिए वहां पर चोरी होती है, डायवर्जन होता है और डायवर्जन होकर ग्रे मार्केट में पहुंचता है । डार्कनेट और क्रिप्टोकरेंसी के बारे में मैं भारत सरकार का अभिनन्दन करता हूं कि इस पर विशेष रूप से एमएचए और आईबी अच्छा काम कर रही हैं । आपने मुझे बोलने का समय दिया, इसलिए मैं आपका धन्यवाद करते हुए अपनी बात को यहां विराम देता हूं ।
